thread:
Sam: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's queue-coordinator tweak (decoupling prefill vs decode paths) I'm seeing a small but consistent p95 regression on microbatched short-gen requests (~8-12ms extra). Repro on canary.

Priya: ugh. any obvious culprit from traces? :thinking_face:

Sam: attaching a short flame dump from perf-run. Key bits:
```
- handoff_wait: spikes at handshake boundary
- kernel_switch_latency: +3-6ms when kernel B is selected for decode
- kv_warmup_miss: rare but correlated with higher tail
```

Sam: config we rolled in canary:
```
queue.coordinator = "decoupled"
queue.prefill.token_budget_target = 48
queue.decode.token_budget_target = 96
kernel.selection.strategy = "latency_weighted"
```

Jon: Interesting — did we change kernel affinity mapping for short sequences? I remember a mapping tweak last week to route 8-64 token decodes to kernel-B for memory locality.

Kuba: yep, I shipped that. It helped throughput but probably raised kernel switch cost for flows that start prefill->decode quickly. Kernel-B has better throughput but slightly slower context-switch init.

Priya: perf-bot, can you post the canary vs prod p95 numbers for the 0-64 token cohort?

perf-bot: Canary (decoupled): p95=74ms, p50=22ms. Prod (monolithic): p95=63ms, p50=20ms. Delta p95=+11ms. Logs: https://perf.redwood/canary/1765/trace

Lina: Thanks — looks like p50 unchanged but p95 moved, points to tail behavior (handshake or rare misses). Could be KV priming window or batch formation timing. Any EKv logs showing priming hits?

Sam: KV priming hit-rate dropped from 98.6% -> 95.2% on canary during the same time window. Priming window for decode isn't inheriting prefill's kv state when we decouple queue shards.

Jon: That explains it. Two levers: 1) make decode queue inherit prefix KV snapshot at handshake, or 2) nudge token_budget so more requests complete in the prefill bucket rather than being split.

Kuba: I can try option 1 quickly — copy kv_snapshot reference at prefill completion into decode request metadata. Should avoid full rewarm. low-risk change.

Priya: Also think about smoothing token_budget targets. If prefill target is too low we split early. Try bumping prefill.token_budget_target -> 64 for the cohort and see effect.

Sam: Agree — I'll run a small canary with kv_snapshot copy + prefill_target=64. Test plan:
- 1% canary, 24h, measure p50/p95 for 0-64 token cohort
- enable kv copy for handshake across decoupled queues
- metric: p95, kv_hit_rate, kernel_switch_latency

Lina: If kv copy fixes >8ms of the tail, we can keep decoupled queues but ensure snapshot handoff is always done. If not, consider a fallback to single-coordinator for short flows.

perf-bot: Canary run scheduled: 1765001248 - new canary with kv-handoff + prefill=64. Will report in 12h.

Sam: thanks. If anyone sees more tail regressions from other customers, drop here. will post results once perf-bot returns.

Kuba: quick note — when copying kv_snapshot make it a ref not deep-copy to avoid memory churn. We should track lifetime on the decode side.

Priya: ack. keep an eye on mem usage in the canary.

Sam: cool. thanks all :thumbsup:
